patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — PrestaShop and Webflow share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose PrestaShop only if your buying job matches “Open-source PHP commerce — Classic free; Hosted from ~$26/mo annual (€24 excl. VAT) with 1” rather than Webflow's shape. Choose Webflow only if your buying job matches “Design-led website platform with Ecommerce — Standard $29/mo (500 items, 2% fee), Plus $74” rather than PrestaShop's shape. Workflow advantage: PrestaShop leans catalog-management; Webflow leans website-builder-commerce. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — PrestaShop and Webflow share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: PrestaShop is Open-source PHP commerce — Classic free; Hosted from ~$26/mo annual (€24 excl. VAT) with 14-day trial; Enterprise quote. WooCommerce keeps t; Webflow is Design-led website platform with Ecommerce — Standard $29/mo (500 items, 2% fee), Plus $74 highlighted (5,000 items, 0% fee), Advanced $212 .
- Company-size focus: PrestaShop (small-business, mid-market) vs Webflow (solo, micro, small-business).
- Workflow coverage skew: PrestaShop-leaning catalog-management vs Webflow-leaning website-builder-commerce.
- Researched limits: PrestaShop — Classic TCO (hosting, modules, agency) is not $0 even when the license is free; Webflow — Ecommerce requires a Site plan in addition to the Ecommerce plan — model combined TCO, not the $29 floor alone.

Limitations — PrestaShop: Classic TCO (hosting, modules, agency) is not $0 even when the license is free; POS / omnichannel is module-dependent, not a native retail bundle; Webflow: Ecommerce requires a Site plan in addition to the Ecommerce plan — model combined TCO, not the $29 floor alone; Catalog caps (500 / 5,000 / 15,000 items) and Standard’s 2% transaction fee trail Shopify-class commerce OS depth.

Poor-fit cases: PrestaShop is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Classic TCO (hosting, modules, agency) is not $0 even when the license is free · Webflow is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Ecommerce requires a Site plan in addition to the Ecommerce plan — model combined TCO, not the $29 floor alone · Avoid PrestaShop if you actually need Webflow's motion (Design-led website platform with Ecommerce — Standard $29/mo (500 items, 2% fee))

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
